learningObjective: Pick an App Service plan tier. Scale up and out, by hand and with autoscale. Create web apps with the right runtime and settings.
engineer: Tiers, smallest to biggest: Free, shared servers, no custom domains; Shared, shared servers, custom domains but no TLS certificates; Basic, your own servers, custom domains and TLS, up to 3 instances (scale by hand only); Standard, autoscale up to 10 instances, 5 deployment slots, backups; Premium v3, up to 30 instances, 20 slots, faster hardware, zone redundancy; Isolated v2 (App Service Environment), up to 100 instances, in your own network.
A plan is a set of servers: it's in one region and one OS (Windows or Linux). Every app on the plan runs on every instance. One busy app slows down the others, so give heavy apps their own plan.
Scale up vs scale out: scale up means a bigger tier. Scale out means more instances.

Ways to scale out: by hand (set the instance count); rule-based autoscale, Standard and above, using the same Azure Monitor autoscale as scale sets (VMSS), with metrics such as CPU, memory or HTTP queue length, and schedules; automatic scaling, Premium only, where Azure decides for you.
Creating an app: a name, which becomes <name>.azurewebsites.net and must be unique; code or container; runtime stack and version; OS; region; plan.

App settings: app settings and connection strings, which your code reads as environment variables; general settings (Always On, HTTP version, ARR affinity); deployment, from ZIP deploy, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps or a container image.
Moving an app to another plan: allowed, if the new plan is in the same resource group and region.

example.title: Putting small sites together
body: Five quiet marketing sites share one Standard S1 plan, which is cheaper than five plans. The busy checkout API gets its own Premium v3 plan, with autoscale from 3 to 20 instances and zone redundancy.

architectureDecisions: Group apps into plans by load and lifecycle: quiet apps can share, busy apps get their own plan.
Production: Premium v3 with zone redundancy.
Apps that must stay warm: turn on Always On, so they don't go idle.

misconceptions.myth: Each app has its own instances.
misconceptions.reality: No. All apps on a plan share its instances.
No. Scaling up changes the tier. Scaling out adds instances.

comparisons.difference: Functions can run on App Service plans too, but they run code in response to events.
Managed app hosting. An App Service plan is a set of VMs you choose and pay for directly.

troubleshooting.cause: The plan is Free or Shared.
troubleshooting.fix: Scale up to Basic or higher.

troubleshooting.symptom: One app slows down every app on the plan.
troubleshooting.fix: Move the heavy app to its own plan.

configuration.limits: Instances: Basic 3, Standard 10, Premium v3 30, Isolated v2 100
configuration.permissions: Website Contributor, Web Plan Contributor, or Contributor
configuration.prerequisites: A resource group and a region
